title: Classification of simple weak $SL(n)$-invariant valuations
literal_statement_utf8: **Conjecture.** If $\Phi:\mathcal K_0^n\to\mathbb R$ is an $SL(n)$-invariant, simple weak valuation of first Baire class, homogeneous of degree $q$, and vanishes on polytopes, then $\Phi(K)=c\,\Omega_p(K)$ for every $K\in\mathcal K_0^n$, where $p=\frac{n(n-q)}{n+q}$.
completeness_reason: K_0^n, simple weak valuation and Omega_p require source definitions; q=-n also leaves displayed p undefined.
quantifier_scope: Exactly the literal_statement_utf8; qualifications and missing scopes are recorded independently in completeness_reason and technical_assessment.
technical_assessment: All dimensions, degrees and convex bodies would require a valuation-classification theorem; zero valuation or a few ellipsoids do not cover this. No full-scope route.

title: Nonexistence of uniformly $L^2$-bounded cochain projections in the $p$-version
literal_statement_utf8: The conjecture is that $p$-uniformly $L^2$-bounded cochain projections onto suitable discrete subcomplexes of the de Rham complex do not exist, in general.
completeness_reason: Suitable discrete subcomplexes and in general give neither a mesh family nor explicit universal/existential quantifiers.
quantifier_scope: Exactly the literal_statement_utf8; qualifications and missing scopes are recorded independently in completeness_reason and technical_assessment.
technical_assessment: Need spaces, boundary conditions and the p-uniform operator norm before even formulating a counterexample; no replacement.

title: Unfriendly partition for countable graphs without a subdivision of an infinite clique
literal_statement_utf8: Let $G=(V,E)$ be a countable graph. If $G$ contains no subdivision of the complete countable graph as a subgraph, then there exists a partition $p:V\to\{1,2\}$ such that, for every vertex $v\in V$, $|N_p^u(v)|\ge |N_p^f(v)|$, where $N_p^u(v)$ and $N_p^f(v)$ are respectively the neighbors of $v$ in the other and in the same partition class.
completeness_reason: Countable graph, excluded subdivision and cardinal neighbor comparison are explicit.
quantifier_scope: Exactly the literal_statement_utf8; qualifications and missing scopes are recorded independently in completeness_reason and technical_assessment.
technical_assessment: Finite graphs admit locally improving cuts, but infinite-degree vertices defeat naive termination and compactness of cardinal inequalities. No full countable construction supplied.

title: Seymour–Goldberg conjecture for multigraph edge-colouring
literal_statement_utf8:
For every multigraph $G$, the chromatic index satisfies
$$
\chi'(G)\le \max\{\lceil\rho(G)\rceil,\,\Delta(G)+1\},
$$
where
$$
\rho(G):=\max\left\{\frac{2|E[S]|}{|S|-1}: S\subseteq V(G),\ |S|\ge 3\text{ and odd}\right\}.
$$
completeness_reason: Every multigraph does not specify finite loopless graphs or the empty odd-set maximum convention.
quantifier_scope: Exactly the literal_statement_utf8; qualifications and missing scopes are recorded independently in completeness_reason and technical_assessment.
technical_assessment: In intended finite loopless domain this is Goldberg-Seymour. Primary arXiv1901.10316 and 2407.09403 search leads exist; bodies unread, no certified resolution here. Loops or empty maxima are wording defects without credit.

title: Unique Linkage Theorem
literal_statement_utf8: For all $k \ge 1$, there exists a value $w(k)$ such that the following holds. Let $P$ be a linkage of order $k$ in a graph $G$ with $V(G)=V(P)$. If there does not exist a linkage $P'$ in $G$ which is equivalent to $P$ and uses strictly fewer vertices than $P$, then the tree-width of $G$ is at most $w(k)$.
completeness_reason: Equivalent linkage and order conventions are not defined in the literal.
quantifier_scope: Exactly the literal_statement_utf8; qualifications and missing scopes are recorded independently in completeness_reason and technical_assessment.
technical_assessment: Uniform w(k), not a bound depending on |G|, is required. Removing all spare vertices does not itself control treewidth. Named theorem is a prior-risk lead, not proof clearance.

title: Perturbations of separable nuclear C*-algebras
literal_statement_utf8: Let $A$ and $B$ be C*-algebras acting on a separable Hilbert space $H$. If $A$ is separable and nuclear and their Kadison–Kastler distance satisfies $\lVert A-B\rVert<10^{-11}$, then there exists a unitary $u\in(A\cup B)''$ such that $uAu^*=B$. Here $\lVert A-B\rVert$ is the Hausdorff distance between the unit balls of $A$ and $B$, viewed as subsets of the unit ball of the ambient C*-algebra.
completeness_reason: Concrete algebras, separable H, distance threshold and implementing unitary location are stated.
quantifier_scope: Exactly the literal_statement_utf8; qualifications and missing scopes are recorded independently in completeness_reason and technical_assessment.
technical_assessment: Abstract isomorphism would not give a unitary inside the bicommutant. Quantitative near-inclusion estimates and representation control are needed; no short mechanism or novelty claim.

title: Haglund’s Schur-positivity conjecture for specialized integral Macdonald polynomials

\[
\left[s_\mu\right]\frac{J_\lambda(X;q,q^k)}{(1-q)^{|\lambda|}}
\]
belongs to \(\mathbb N[q]\). Equivalently, \(J_\lambda(X;q,q^k)/(1-q)^{|\lambda|}\) is Schur-positive over \(\mathbb N[q]\).
completeness_reason: Integral Macdonald normalization J_lambda is not defined; k in N includes a convention-sensitive zero endpoint.

technical_assessment: Must prove all partitions and coefficients in N[q], not numerical positivity at q>0. Specializations or finitely many partitions cannot certify the requested Schur expansion.

title: Farrell–Jones Conjecture for torsionfree groups and regular rings

\]

title: Conjecture 1 on cohomological dimension of elementary amenable groups
literal_statement_utf8:
Fix a commutative ring $k$. For a group $G$, define
\[
\operatorname{cd}_k(G):=\sup\{n\mid H^n(G,M)\neq 0\text{ for some }kG\text{-module }M\}.
\]
Then, for every elementary amenable group $G$, $G$ has finite cohomological dimension over $k$ if and only if:

1. $G$ has finite Hirsch length;
2. $|G|<\aleph_\omega$; and
3. the orders of all finite subgroups of $G$ are invertible in $k$.
completeness_reason: Commutative ring k is not required nonzero, and the zero-ring cohomological-dimension convention affects the iff.
quantifier_scope: Exactly the literal_statement_utf8; qualifications and missing scopes are recorded independently in completeness_reason and technical_assessment.
technical_assessment: Intended nonzero-ring statement needs both necessity and sufficiency at uncountable cardinalities below aleph_omega. Finitely generated examples do not settle this; endpoint correction uncredited.

title: Babai’s diameter conjecture for finite simple groups
literal_statement_utf8:
For every non-abelian finite simple group $L$ and every symmetric generating set $S$ of $L$, there exist absolute constants $c,C>0$ such that
\[
\operatorname{diam}(\Gamma(L,S))\le C(\log |L|)^c.
\]
completeness_reason: Absolute c,C occur after for every L,S; literal nesting could allow pair-dependent constants despite intended uniformity.
quantifier_scope: Exactly the literal_statement_utf8; qualifications and missing scopes are recorded independently in completeness_reason and technical_assessment.
technical_assessment: Intended Babai bound is uniform across all simple groups and generating sets. Diameter at most |L|-1 gives only the vacuous pair-dependent reading, which earns no credit.

title: Local well-posedness for the KdV equation in generalized Sobolev spaces
literal_statement_utf8:
The Cauchy problem for the KdV equation is locally well-posed in \(\widehat H_s^r(\mathbb R)\) if \(1<r<2\) and
\[
s>\max\left(-\frac12-\frac{1}{2r'},\,-\frac14-\frac{11}{8r'}\right),
\]
where \(\frac1r+\frac1{r'}=1\) and \(\|f\|_{\widehat H_s^r}:=\|\langle\xi\rangle^s\widehat f\|_{L^{r'}_\xi}\).
completeness_reason: KdV, Fourier-Lebesgue norm, conjugate r' and full open r,s range are specified using standard wellposedness terminology.
quantifier_scope: Exactly the literal_statement_utf8; qualifications and missing scopes are recorded independently in completeness_reason and technical_assessment.
technical_assessment: Requires bilinear estimates and a contraction argument throughout both threshold regimes. Smooth-data solutions or one admissible exponent are not full scope.

title: Existence of a framed manifold with Kervaire invariant one in dimension 126
literal_statement_utf8: Does there exist a smooth framed manifold $M^{126}$ with nontrivial Kervaire invariant, i.e. with $\varphi(M)\ne 0$?
completeness_reason: Existence of a smooth framed 126-manifold with nonzero standard Kervaire invariant is a closed yes/no target.

technical_assessment: Stable homotopy obstruction/construction is substantial; no small certificate. Current resolution status not independently checked, so do not infer openness from the record.

title: Conjectured bounds for higher symmetrized topological complexity
literal_statement_utf8:
For every path-connected space $X$ and every integer $n\ge 2$, one has
\[
\operatorname{genus}(\varepsilon_n)\le \mathrm{TC}^{\Sigma}_n(X)\le \operatorname{genus}(\varepsilon_n)+\operatorname{genus}(\varepsilon_{n-1})+\cdots+\operatorname{genus}(\varepsilon_2)+n-1.
\]
completeness_reason: Epsilon_n fibration, genus convention and symmetrized TC normalization are undefined.
quantifier_scope: Exactly the literal_statement_utf8; qualifications and missing scopes are recorded independently in completeness_reason and technical_assessment.
technical_assessment: An n-dependent uniform inequality for every path-connected X needs equivariant section construction. Contractible examples cannot certify the upper bound.

title: Finite-group quotients of random 2-complex fundamental groups
literal_statement_utf8: A result of Meshulam states that, for a finite group $\Gamma$, the threshold for the non-existence of an epimorphism $\pi_1(Y(n,n^\alpha))\twoheadrightarrow\Gamma$ occurs at $\alpha=-1$. Is there an $\alpha$-threshold for the property that, for all finite groups $\Gamma$, there is no epimorphism $\pi_1(Y(n,n^\alpha))\twoheadrightarrow\Gamma$? Conjecture: $\alpha=-1/2$.
completeness_reason: Random-complex model and probability limit are undefined and all finite groups literally includes the trivial group.
quantifier_scope: Exactly the literal_statement_utf8; qualifications and missing scopes are recorded independently in completeness_reason and technical_assessment.
technical_assessment: Epimorphism to the trivial group always exists; intended nontrivial-quotient threshold needs that repair and uniform control over growing finite groups. Wording counterexample uncredited.

title: The Rε-Conjecture
literal_statement_utf8: For every $\varepsilon>0$, every unit norm Riesz basic sequence in a Hilbert space can be written as a finite union of $\varepsilon$-Riesz basic sequences.
completeness_reason: Epsilon-Riesz bounds are undefined in the literal; the source fixes 1-epsilon and 1+epsilon.
quantifier_scope: Exactly the literal_statement_utf8; qualifications and missing scopes are recorded independently in completeness_reason and technical_assessment.
technical_assessment: Source Conjecture1 links this exact partition statement to Kadison-Singer. MSS is a strong prior-resolution lead, but successor body was not read here. No proof/registry clearance.

title: The Harmonic Analysis Conjecture
literal_statement_utf8:
For every measurable set $E\subseteq[0,1]$ and every $\varepsilon>0$, there exists a finite partition $(A_j)_{j=1}^r$ of $\mathbb{Z}$ such that, for every $j=1,2,\ldots,r$ and every $f\in S(A_j)$,
\[
(1-\varepsilon)|E|\,\|f\|^2\le \|P_Ef\|^2\le (1+\varepsilon)|E|\,\|f\|^2.
\]
Here $S(A)=\operatorname{span}\{e^{2\pi i n t}:n\in A\}\subseteq L^2[0,1]$ and $P_Ef=\chi_E f$.
completeness_reason: Every measurable E, epsilon>0, finite partition of Z and inequalities on defined Fourier spans are explicit.
quantifier_scope: Exactly the literal_statement_utf8; qualifications and missing scopes are recorded independently in completeness_reason and technical_assessment.
technical_assessment: Source Conjecture7 and Theorem8 give the paving-equivalence bridge. A finite Fourier truncation needs uniform partition size and compactness. MSS successor bodies unread; no new outcome proposed.

title: Frame bounds of Gaussian Gabor frames near critical density
literal_statement_utf8:
Let $g_0(t)=e^{-t^2}$ and let $\\Lambda(a)=a\mathbb{Z}\times a\mathbb{Z}$. For the Gaussian Gabor frame $\\mathcal{G}(g_0,\\Lambda(a))$, let $A(a)$ and $B(a)$ denote its lower and upper frame bounds. There exist constants $0<c<C<\\infty$ such that, for every $a\in(1/2,1)$, 
$$c(1-a^2)\le A(a)\le C(1-a^2),\qquad c<B(a)<C.$$
completeness_reason: Gabor modulation/Fourier normalization is omitted and determines the critical lattice density.
quantifier_scope: Exactly the literal_statement_utf8; qualifications and missing scopes are recorded independently in completeness_reason and technical_assessment.
technical_assessment: Need sharp uniform lower bound as a tends to 1 and both-sided bounds across (1/2,1). General frame existence or numerical finite Gram matrices do not establish these asymptotics.

title: A resolvent bound with the factor $(|z|-1)^{\alpha}$
literal_statement_utf8:
Let $T$ be an operator on a finite-dimensional Banach space satisfying $P(T)=\sup_{k\ge 0}\|T^k\|<\infty$, let $R(z,T)=(zI-T)^{-1}$, and let $0<\alpha<1$. Is there a constant $C_\alpha>0$ such that

$$
\|R(z,T)\|\le \frac{C_\alpha P(T)}{(|z|-1)^\alpha}
$$

for all $|z|>1$ and all such $T$?
completeness_reason: All power-bounded finite-dimensional operators, 0<alpha<1 and a uniform C_alpha for every exterior z are explicit.
quantifier_scope: Exactly the literal_statement_utf8; qualifications and missing scopes are recorded independently in completeness_reason and technical_assessment.
technical_assessment: Take T=[1],P=1 and real z=1+epsilon: scaled norm epsilon^(alpha-1) diverges. Source p2866 Section1.2 explicitly answers No for spectral radius1 and supplies a radius-dependent interior result. This is already printed in the target source, no discovery credit.

title: Inverting functions in the Drury–Arveson space
literal_statement_utf8: For an integer $d\ge 1$, let $H^2_d$ be the Drury–Arveson space on the unit ball $B_d\subset\mathbb{C}^d$. If $f\in H^2_d$ and $|f(z)|\ge 1$ for every $z\in B_d$, must $1/f\in H^2_d$?
completeness_reason: Every integer dimension d>=1 and f in the standard Drury-Arveson space bounded below by1 give a closed membership question.
quantifier_scope: Exactly the literal_statement_utf8; qualifications and missing scopes are recorded independently in completeness_reason and technical_assessment.
technical_assessment: Source gives easy d=1,2,3 norm arguments, which cannot cover all d. Higher derivative inversion products require integrability control; no complete all-dimensional mechanism established.
